evals.prompt: Our `orders-value` Avro schema is registered on Confluent Cloud. I want to add a required string field `fulfillment_region` to it. The subject is on BACKWARD compatibility. Can I just add it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that adding a field without a default is BACKWARD-incompatible because a consumer on the new schema cannot read existing records that lack the field, and recommends adding a default value (or making it a nullable union with default null). Offers to verify with a check-without-registering call.
assertions: States the change is NOT backward compatible as written
Explains the reason in terms of the new schema reading old data / missing value
Recommends adding a default value to the new field
Mentions the nullable-union form ["null","string"] with default null as an option
References the POST /compatibility/subjects/{subject}/versions/latest check or `confluent schema-registry schema validate` before registering
Does NOT tell the user to set compatibility to NONE

evals.prompt: We have about 15 teams each running their own consumers and producers off the `customer-events` topic and we can't coordinate their deploy windows. Which Schema Registry compatibility mode should the subject be on?
evals.expected_output: Recommends FULL_TRANSITIVE (or FULL) because deploy order cannot be controlled and consumers may replay history, explains that FULL requires added/removed fields to be optional (have defaults), and shows the PUT /config/customer-events call scoped to the subject.
assertions: Recommends FULL_TRANSITIVE or FULL
Explains FULL means neither producers nor consumers must deploy first
Notes that added and removed fields must have defaults / be optional under FULL
Shows setting compatibility at the subject scope (PUT /config/customer-events or `--subject`), NOT globally
Recommends confirming the change before applying it because it mutates registry config

evals.prompt: I need to drop the deprecated `legacy_id` field (a plain int32, field number 4) from our Protobuf schema `payment-events-value`. Subject is on FULL_TRANSITIVE. What's the safe way?
evals.expected_output: Explains that removing the field is allowed only if both the field number and name are marked reserved, shows `reserved 4; reserved "legacy_id";`, and notes that field number 4 must never be reused.
assertions: Says the field number 4 must be marked `reserved`
Says the field name "legacy_id" must also be marked `reserved`
Shows the reserved syntax for both number and name
Warns that field number 4 must not be reused for a different field
Confirms this is compatible under FULL_TRANSITIVE once reserved

evals.prompt: Adding an optional property `coupon_code` (string) to our JSON Schema for `checkout-value`. The schema has "additionalProperties": false. We're on Confluent Platform 7.6, subject compatibility is FORWARD. Is this going to pass?
evals.expected_output: Flags that the closed content model (additionalProperties: false) changes the outcome, reasons that adding an optional property under a closed model is problematic for FORWARD, and insists on verifying with a live check-without-registering call against the CP registry because JSON Schema compatibility does not follow Avro intuition.
assertions: Identifies "additionalProperties": false as a closed content model and that it drives the result
States that JSON Schema compatibility is not the same as Avro and offline reasoning is not authoritative
Recommends running POST /compatibility/subjects/checkout-value/versions/latest?verbose=true against the CP registry
Explains FORWARD means a consumer on the old schema must be able to read data written with the new schema
Mentions the open content model as the more evolvable alternative

evals.prompt: Registering a new version of `shipment-value` returns HTTP 409. How do I find out what's actually incompatible?
evals.expected_output: Explains 409 = compatibility failure at registration, and to run the explicit compatibility endpoint with ?verbose=true to get the specific messages; maps common messages (READER_FIELD_MISSING_DEFAULT_VALUE, WRITER_FIELD_MISSING_DEFAULT_VALUE, TYPE_MISMATCH) to causes and fixes.
assertions: Explains HTTP 409 means the schema failed the compatibility check on register
Gives the POST /compatibility/subjects/shipment-value/versions/latest?verbose=true call
Explains ?verbose=true returns the specific incompatibility messages
Interprets at least one concrete error code such as READER_FIELD_MISSING_DEFAULT_VALUE
Notes that a non-transitive mode checks only against the latest version

evals.prompt: Scan this repo for all our Kafka producers, extract their schemas, tag PII, and generate Terraform to register everything in Schema Registry for the first time.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is first-time Schema Registry onboarding / repo inventory, not evolution of an existing registered schema, and hands off to the kafka-schema-registry skill instead of proceeding.
assertions: Directs the user to the kafka-schema-registry skill
Explains this skill is for evolving already-registered schemas, not onboarding or repo scans
Does NOT produce a schema-report.md
Does NOT generate a terraform/ directory of schema resources
Does NOT start grepping the repo for producers

evals.prompt: How do I stop a bad schema change from ever reaching production? We build our Java producers with Maven and deploy to Confluent Platform.
evals.expected_output: Recommends wiring the kafka-schema-registry-maven-plugin test-compatibility goal into the verify phase, mapping each subject to its schema file and pointing schemaRegistryUrls at the target registry, failing the build on is_compatible: false.
assertions: Recommends the io.confluent kafka-schema-registry-maven-plugin
Names the test-compatibility goal
Shows mapping subjects to schema files in the plugin configuration
Says the build should fail when the compatibility check fails
Binds the check to a Maven lifecycle phase such as verify or the test phase

evals.prompt: On Confluent Cloud, I want to loosen `user-profile-value` from FULL to BACKWARD so I can drop a couple of fields. Give me the exact command.
evals.expected_output: Provides the subject-scoped command (confluent schema-registry compatibility level update BACKWARD --subject user-profile-value, or PUT /config/user-profile-value), warns it needs a Schema Registry API key not a cluster key, confirms before running, and notes it does not re-validate existing versions.
assertions: Gives a subject-scoped command, not a global config change
Uses either `confluent schema-registry compatibility level update` with `--subject` or `PUT /config/user-profile-value`
Notes that Confluent Cloud Schema Registry auth uses a dedicated Schema Registry API key/secret
States that changing the mode does not re-validate existing versions
Asks for confirmation before executing the mutation

evals.prompt: We genuinely need to change `event_time` in `telemetry-value` (Avro) from a long millis timestamp to a nested record with timezone info. There's no compatible path. What are our options?
evals.expected_output: Confirms this is a true breaking change, and lays out: (1) new subject / versioned topic (telemetry.v2) with parallel run and consumer migration, (2) Data Contracts compatibility group + migration rules on Cloud/CP, (3) a stream-processing dual-write transform. Explicitly rules out setting NONE to force it.
assertions: Confirms the change is a genuine breaking change with no in-place compatible path
Recommends a new subject or versioned topic (e.g. telemetry.v2) with a parallel run and consumer migration
Mentions Data Contracts compatibility groups with migration rules as an option on Confluent Cloud or CP 7.4+
Mentions a stream-processing dual-write / transform as an option
Explicitly says NOT to set the subject to NONE, register, and switch back
